mystara.rule.dual-classes.name: Dual Classes

effect.summary: Some humanoids may learn both wicca and shaman crafts.

mystara.rule.dual-classes.cost_or_limit: Level limits for both crafts are halved, and the character must meet both experience costs; each character can have only one subordinate-teacher relationship.
mystara.rule.dual-classes.go_wrong: Teachers may compete and pressure the apprentice to abandon the other craft; exceeding the reduced limit prevents starting the second craft later.
mystara.rule.dual-classes.who_may: Humanoids whose teachers permit dual study, or who learn crafts at different career stages within the limits.
mystara.rule.dual-classes.blocked_reason: The rule modifies advancement limits and costs rather than requiring an unavailable effect.

mystara.rule.excessive-amulets-attract-e.name: Excessive amulets attract entities

effect.summary: Each time an amulet is used, a character with multiple amulets risks attracting an outer-plane entity that may steal one or possess the owner.

mystara.rule.excessive-amulets-attract-e.cost_or_limit: The chance is 1% per existing amulet; a stolen amulet increases the daily save penalty by one.
mystara.rule.excessive-amulets-attract-e.go_wrong: The entity may control the owner; destroying the tampered amulet or amulets frees the victim.
mystara.rule.excessive-amulets-attract-e.mind: The entity may possess and control the owner.
mystara.rule.excessive-amulets-attract-e.where_from: The soul fragments held in amulets attract outer-plane entities.
mystara.rule.excessive-amulets-attract-e.combines: Amulet use and destruction; stolen items affect daily saving throws.
mystara.rule.excessive-amulets-attract-e.blocked_reason: The rule makes an item’s soul fragment a target for possession and control.

mystara.rule.jammudaru-cauldron-rite.name: Jammudaru cauldron rite

effect.summary: A shaman cooks a foe alive in a gri-gri cauldron, then consumes it at one Hit Die per turn.

mystara.rule.jammudaru-cauldron-rite.cost_or_limit: The foe must fit alive in the cauldron; the shaman must howl incantations.
mystara.rule.jammudaru-cauldron-rite.go_wrong: The foe dies during the cooking and consumption process.
mystara.rule.jammudaru-cauldron-rite.combines: The remaining goo can be used to prepare Juju Moss.
mystara.rule.jammudaru-cauldron-rite.blocked_reason: The description relies on a specific cooking-and-consumption ritual rather than a basic effect.

mystara.rule.reincarnation-into-humanoid.name: Reincarnation into humanoid bodies

effect.summary: The most chaotic or evil beings are reborn as humanoids to suffer and atone.

mystara.rule.reincarnation-into-humanoid.cost_or_limit: This fate applies to especially evil souls, according to the account.
mystara.rule.reincarnation-into-humanoid.go_wrong: The reborn endure hardship and may not know their origin.
mystara.rule.reincarnation-into-humanoid.mind: Past-life knowledge is hidden until a high level and a shamanic ritual reveal it.
mystara.rule.reincarnation-into-humanoid.who_may: Souls of beings judged sufficiently evil.
mystara.rule.reincarnation-into-humanoid.where_from: The design attributed to the lords of the four spheres.
mystara.rule.reincarnation-into-humanoid.combines: A powerful humanoid may learn the truth through dreams and a shaman or wicca ritual.
mystara.rule.reincarnation-into-humanoid.blocked_reason: The rule defines souls being reborn and past-life memories being revealed.

mystara.rule.humanoids-sacred-land.name: Humanoids’ Sacred Land

effect.summary: The Broken Lands were made deadly for the reincarnated tribes, and uninvited entrants are said to face death by orcish blade.

mystara.rule.humanoids-sacred-land.cost_or_limit: The region has dangerous terrain, climate, and gas clouds.
mystara.rule.humanoids-sacred-land.go_wrong: Uninvited entrants are threatened with death.
mystara.rule.humanoids-sacred-land.who_may: Humanoid tribes inhabit the land; outsiders are unwelcome.
mystara.rule.humanoids-sacred-land.where_from: The Immortals’ shaping of the region.
mystara.rule.humanoids-sacred-land.combines: Linked to the reincarnation purpose of humanoids.
mystara.rule.humanoids-sacred-land.blocked_reason: The rule combines a region-wide environmental hazard with a territorial prohibition.

mystara.rule.shaman-and-wicca-apprentice.name: Shaman and wicca apprenticeship

effect.summary: A prospective practitioner must serve as a spellcaster’s subordinate for at least one full level-advancement period.

mystara.rule.shaman-and-wicca-apprentice.cost_or_limit: Shamans require Wisdom 9 and wiccas Intelligence 9; abilities begin no earlier than first level.
mystara.rule.shaman-and-wicca-apprentice.where_from: A teacher of the chosen craft.
mystara.rule.shaman-and-wicca-apprentice.combines: The same teacher relationship constrains dual-craft study.
mystara.rule.shaman-and-wicca-apprentice.blocked_reason: The requirement is a straightforward prerequisite and time cost.

mystara.rule.spellcasting-does-not-chang.name: Spellcasting does not change combat ability

effect.summary: Gaining spellcasting does not change the character’s hit points or combat abilities.

mystara.rule.spellcasting-does-not-chang.cost_or_limit: Saving throws may instead use the better spellcaster-class values.
mystara.rule.spellcasting-does-not-chang.combines: Compares the character’s normal saves with wizard or cleric saves.
mystara.rule.spellcasting-does-not-chang.blocked_reason: This is a direct restriction on advancement effects.

mystara.rule.permanent-spellcasting-reti.name: Permanent spellcasting retirement

effect.summary: A character who permanently stops improving a craft gains no further spellcasting powers from it.

mystara.rule.permanent-spellcasting-reti.cost_or_limit: The decision is final and irreversible; normal humanoid experience requirements then resume.
mystara.rule.permanent-spellcasting-reti.go_wrong: Further craft advancement cannot be resumed.
mystara.rule.permanent-spellcasting-reti.who_may: A spellcaster choosing to stop advancement.
mystara.rule.permanent-spellcasting-reti.combines: Requires recalculating the character’s experience table.
mystara.rule.permanent-spellcasting-reti.blocked_reason: The rule permanently alters whether a character can acquire a power progression.

mystara.rule.spell-recovery-by-ritual.name: Spell recovery by ritual

effect.summary: Wiccas and shamans recover spells through dancing, shouting, howling, and waving gri-gris rather than conventional study or prayer.

mystara.rule.spell-recovery-by-ritual.cost_or_limit: No specific recovery duration is stated.
mystara.rule.spell-recovery-by-ritual.blocked_reason: Recovery is linked to the required gri-gri implement.

mystara.rule.gri-gri-attunement-and-loca.name: Gri-gri attunement and location sense

effect.summary: The passage ritual sends shreds of the caster into the gri-gri, attuning it so only its owner can use it and sense it within 100 feet.

mystara.rule.gri-gri-attunement-and-loca.cost_or_limit: The caster can have any number of gri-gris.
mystara.rule.gri-gri-attunement-and-loca.go_wrong: Destroying one permanently costs 1d4 hit points; a lost one requires repeating the passage ritual to replace it.
mystara.rule.gri-gri-attunement-and-loca.combines: The implement is required for spellcasting.
mystara.rule.gri-gri-attunement-and-loca.blocked_reason: The mechanism puts a fragment of the owner into an item and binds its use and location to that owner.

mystara.rule.troll-personal-sacrifice.name: Troll personal sacrifice

effect.summary: Trolls double the effects whenever they roll on the Personal Sacrifice Table.

mystara.rule.troll-personal-sacrifice.cost_or_limit: Applies to trolls making such a roll.

mystara.rule.death-scars-and-yagrai-revi.name: Death Scars and Yagrai revival

effect.summary: Yagrai shaman status requires twelve Death Scars; follower resistance improves with each ten scars, up to a +5 bonus.

mystara.rule.death-scars-and-yagrai-revi.cost_or_limit: Revival also requires a successful Wisdom check and is limited to the specified negative hit-point threshold.
mystara.rule.death-scars-and-yagrai-revi.blocked_reason: The rule governs revival after a fatal blow, a death-state capability outside the basic effect grammar.

mystara.rule.skinwing-carrying-limits.name: Skinwing carrying limits

effect.summary: Skinwings can carry up to 600 pounds, with increasing danger when carrying over 300 pounds across lava.

mystara.rule.skinwing-carrying-limits.cost_or_limit: A 10% chance of falling for every eight miles when over 300 pounds; cannot lift more than 600 pounds.

mystara.rule.xilochtli-s-heart-and-contr.name: Xilochtli's heart and control

effect.summary: Xilochtli can be killed only by destroying his external heart; whoever possesses the heart's jar can control him.

mystara.rule.xilochtli-s-heart-and-contr.cost_or_limit: The heart is held in a matching temple in the Sphere of Entropy.
mystara.rule.xilochtli-s-heart-and-contr.go_wrong: Destroying the heart kills him; possession grants control.
mystara.rule.xilochtli-s-heart-and-contr.mind: The holder can control Xilochtli completely.
mystara.rule.xilochtli-s-heart-and-contr.who_may: Whoever possesses the jar and heart
mystara.rule.xilochtli-s-heart-and-contr.combines: The heart is separate from his body.
mystara.rule.xilochtli-s-heart-and-contr.blocked_reason: This rule defines a remote life-state and control link that the basic effect grammar cannot model.

mystara.rule.rabid-zar-s-attack.name: Rabid Zar’s attack

effect.summary: At half hit points or less, Zar attacks the nearest man-like being and maintains a damaging bite until stopped.

mystara.rule.rabid-zar-s-attack.cost_or_limit: Triggers when Zar loses half or more of his hit points; bite ends if he is knocked unconscious or reduced to zero hit points.
mystara.rule.rabid-zar-s-attack.go_wrong: The target may be infected; a sufficiently powerful cleric can cure the disease.
mystara.rule.rabid-zar-s-attack.blocked_reason: The rule specifies a hit-point-triggered behavioral change and its continuing bite, which the basic effect grammar cannot fully model.

mystara.rule.chief-checks.name: Chief checks

effect.summary: An Authority or Servility check succeeds on a d8 result at or below the relevant level; an 8 always fails.

mystara.rule.chief-checks.cost_or_limit: One eight-sided die and the listed rating.
mystara.rule.chief-checks.go_wrong: A failed check can cause disobedience, desertion, or other specified consequences.
mystara.rule.chief-checks.who_may: Chiefs subject to an Authority or Servility check.

mystara.rule.captured-chiefs.name: Captured chiefs

effect.summary: Captured chiefs can be ransomed, transferred to a new owner, or executed and returned to the counter cup.

mystara.rule.captured-chiefs.cost_or_limit: A captured chief remains with the captor until combat ends.
mystara.rule.captured-chiefs.go_wrong: A caravan carrying a chief executes him on reaching its destination.
mystara.rule.captured-chiefs.who_may: Chiefs captured in combat or by a caravan.
mystara.rule.captured-chiefs.combines: Ransoms may exchange gold, counters, territories, or hordes.
mystara.rule.captured-chiefs.blocked_reason: The procedure changes ownership of a captured chief and can end in execution, not represented by basic effects.

mystara.rule.territory-control.name: Territory control

effect.summary: A coalition claims a Broken Lands territory by placing a chief there or conquering it; control can persist while empty.

mystara.rule.territory-control.cost_or_limit: Only Broken Lands territories can be controlled.
mystara.rule.territory-control.go_wrong: Control can be lost when the territory becomes neutral or is taken by an enemy.

mystara.rule.levying-hordes.name: Levying hordes

effect.summary: Counters are placed from a player’s hand, with chiefs and hordes restricted to their native territories and other placement conditions.

mystara.rule.levying-hordes.cost_or_limit: A chief must be present or placed simultaneously with its hordes.
mystara.rule.levying-hordes.go_wrong: A failed Authority check when taking over other-race hordes makes them rebel and attack.
mystara.rule.levying-hordes.mind: The check represents command and obedience.
mystara.rule.levying-hordes.combines: May place chiefs, hordes, fortresses, mines, shamans, and war machines.

mystara.rule.neutral-territories.name: Neutral territories

effect.summary: A Broken Lands territory without a coalition owner is neutral; an entering army or chief claims it unless occupants resist.

mystara.rule.neutral-territories.cost_or_limit: Rival occupants require combat or same-race rallying.
mystara.rule.neutral-territories.go_wrong: Neutral hordes may immediately attack armies and chiefs near them.
mystara.rule.neutral-territories.who_may: Any chief or army entering a neutral territory.
mystara.rule.neutral-territories.combines: Uses control markers and the rally rule.

mystara.rule.movement.name: Movement

effect.summary: Armies move one adjacent area per turn, while lone chiefs can cross two unoccupied territories.

mystara.rule.movement.cost_or_limit: Hordes cannot move without a chief; armies stop to claim an unoccupied territory.
mystara.rule.movement.go_wrong: An isolated chief crossing enemy territory risks a forced battle; underground movement can kill or lose an army.
mystara.rule.movement.combines: Fortresses enable underground movement; terrain otherwise does not affect surface movement.

mystara.rule.underground-movement.name: Underground movement

effect.summary: A chief or army in a fortress may attempt to travel underground to another fortress or a random territory.

mystara.rule.underground-movement.cost_or_limit: Requires a fortress and a d20 roll.
mystara.rule.underground-movement.go_wrong: A 20 kills the expedition in a cave-in; a 19 leaves it lost in the dark for another turn.
mystara.rule.underground-movement.who_may: An army or chief in a fortress.
mystara.rule.underground-movement.where_from: Caverns and tunnels beneath the Broken Lands.
mystara.rule.underground-movement.combines: An underground attack negates the defender’s fortress strength.
mystara.rule.underground-movement.blocked_reason: The rule moves units between nonadjacent spaces with random destination and temporary storage in a lost-state box.

mystara.rule.transferring-counters.name: Transferring counters

effect.summary: Friendly armies may meet to transfer hordes, but a new chief must pass an Authority check or transferred hordes turn neutral.

mystara.rule.transferring-counters.cost_or_limit: Armies must end their movement in the same territory.
mystara.rule.transferring-counters.go_wrong: Failed command turns the transferred hordes neutral and they attack nearby armies and chiefs.
mystara.rule.transferring-counters.combines: Uses Authority checks and neutral-horde rules.
mystara.rule.transferring-counters.blocked_reason: Units change command and allegiance, which the basic effect grammar cannot fully model.

mystara.rule.multiple-chief-operations.name: Multiple-Chief Operations

effect.summary: Multiple chiefs can share a territory, but their armies fight separately and in player-chosen order.

mystara.rule.multiple-chief-operations.cost_or_limit: A defeated army’s surviving hordes may be seized by another chief.
mystara.rule.multiple-chief-operations.go_wrong: A defeated chief may flee to another coalition after failing a Servility check.
mystara.rule.multiple-chief-operations.who_may: Coalitions with multiple chiefs in one territory.
mystara.rule.multiple-chief-operations.combines: Uses combat, capture, and Servility checks.
mystara.rule.multiple-chief-operations.blocked_reason: The procedure can change a defeated chief’s coalition membership.

mystara.rule.war-machine-construction.name: War machine construction

effect.summary: Machine quality depends on chief level, and construction requires skills, money, and a year without interruption.

mystara.rule.war-machine-construction.cost_or_limit: Costs 1,000 gp per efficiency level; any travel, raid, or war during construction loses all progress and cost.
mystara.rule.war-machine-construction.go_wrong: Failed checks render the machine unusable and require a restart.
mystara.rule.war-machine-construction.who_may: A chief with Engineering and Artillery skills
mystara.rule.war-machine-construction.combines: Successful completion requires a War Machine and Artillery check.

mystara.rule.fortress-construction-and-d.name: Fortress construction and defense

effect.summary: A fortress costs gold equal to its strength, occupies a friendly territory, and adds its strength to its defenders.

mystara.rule.fortress-construction-and-d.cost_or_limit: Only one per territory; cannot be built while potentially hostile hordes are being levied there.
mystara.rule.fortress-construction-and-d.go_wrong: Does not protect against underground entry or rebellious hordes.
mystara.rule.fortress-construction-and-d.combines: Enables underground movement and modifies checks for native chiefs and outsiders.

mystara.rule.code-of-ethnits.name: Code of Ethnits

effect.summary: A chief leading nonnative hordes must pass an Authority check for each such horde before battle, or it joins the enemy.

mystara.rule.code-of-ethnits.cost_or_limit: Does not apply when chiefs of the same race fight each other.
mystara.rule.code-of-ethnits.go_wrong: Failure causes hordes to change sides.
mystara.rule.code-of-ethnits.blocked_reason: Hordes change allegiance based on a command check, a mind or loyalty interaction outside the basic grammar.

mystara.rule.combat-results.name: Combat results

effect.summary: Combat compares force totals and uses a die and table to determine casualties, retreat, capture, surrender, or exchange.

mystara.rule.combat-results.cost_or_limit: Uses army strengths, eligible machines and fortresses, and a d6 table.
mystara.rule.combat-results.go_wrong: Results can destroy armies, kill chiefs, or force retreats and losses.
mystara.rule.combat-results.mind: Some results use Authority checks for loyalty.
mystara.rule.combat-results.who_may: Armies, chiefs, fortresses, and caravans in combat.
mystara.rule.combat-results.combines: Applies to caravans and territorial attacks as well as armies.

mystara.rule.caravan-movement-and-combat.name: Caravan movement and combat

effect.summary: A caravan advances one space each turn and its carried gold value is also its combat strength.

mystara.rule.caravan-movement-and-combat.cost_or_limit: Routes are fixed and caravans never travel backward.
mystara.rule.caravan-movement-and-combat.go_wrong: Raiding or combat can cost it gold, cause it to flee, or destroy it.
mystara.rule.caravan-movement-and-combat.who_may: Caravans drawn from the Gold Cup.
mystara.rule.caravan-movement-and-combat.combines: Can carry captured chiefs and gold.

mystara.rule.gold-counter-spending.name: Gold counter spending

effect.summary: Gold counters have fixed values and are spent whole, with no change returned.

mystara.rule.gold-counter-spending.cost_or_limit: A counter worth more than a purchase price is still spent entirely.
mystara.rule.gold-counter-spending.combines: Spent counters return to the Gold Cup.

mystara.rule.mine-income.name: Mine income

effect.summary: A mine produces a random gold counter when a horde occupies its area during the relevant turn step.

mystara.rule.mine-income.cost_or_limit: A chief alone cannot mine; only one mine can occupy an area.
mystara.rule.mine-income.go_wrong: Drawing a caravan yields no mine income that turn.
mystara.rule.mine-income.who_may: A horde in a mined territory.
mystara.rule.mine-income.combines: Uses the Gold Cup; a caravan drawn for a neutral mine is placed on the map.

mystara.rule.spy-use-and-treachery.name: Spy use and treachery

effect.summary: A spy may expose or steal counters or help bribe a chief into switching coalitions after a Servility check.

mystara.rule.spy-use-and-treachery.cost_or_limit: The bribe equals the chief’s Servility rating plus the spy’s skill; one chief coalition cannot be targeted for treachery.
mystara.rule.spy-use-and-treachery.go_wrong: Failure costs a bribe counter; success for the spy causes a chief, territory, and counters to change coalition.
mystara.rule.spy-use-and-treachery.mind: The chief’s loyalty is tested and may change.
mystara.rule.spy-use-and-treachery.who_may: Players with a spy and eligible target chief.
mystara.rule.spy-use-and-treachery.combines: A chiefless faction gets a bonus when using a spy.
mystara.rule.spy-use-and-treachery.blocked_reason: The rule enables a chief to switch allegiance and transfer a territory through a loyalty test.

mystara.rule.shaman-bonuses.name: Shaman bonuses

effect.summary: A shaman adds one to its chief’s combat rolls and Authority and Servility checks.

mystara.rule.shaman-bonuses.go_wrong: In neutral territory, its combat bonus benefits local neutral hordes.
mystara.rule.shaman-bonuses.who_may: A chief with an attached shaman.
mystara.rule.shaman-bonuses.combines: Follows the winner of a battle.

mystara.rule.orcs-on-a-rampage.name: Orcs on a Rampage

effect.summary: A raiding army or chief can gain a random loot counter in foreign lands and must carry it to friendly territory.

mystara.rule.orcs-on-a-rampage.cost_or_limit: A lone chief may carry only one gold counter; armies may carry any number.
mystara.rule.orcs-on-a-rampage.go_wrong: A raiding army may lose a random horde and its loot on a failed Authority check.
mystara.rule.orcs-on-a-rampage.mind: The check represents the chief’s command over raiders.
mystara.rule.orcs-on-a-rampage.who_may: An army or chief visiting foreign lands.
mystara.rule.orcs-on-a-rampage.combines: A caravan drawn as loot goes to the player’s hand instead.

mystara.rule.mummification-and-life-afte.name: Mummification and life after death

effect.summary: Oenkmarians commonly believe mummification ensures life after death, and mummies may animate to curse profaners.

mystara.rule.mummification-and-life-afte.cost_or_limit: Burial is in taboo family crypts.
mystara.rule.mummification-and-life-afte.go_wrong: Profaners may face revenge and horrifying curses.
mystara.rule.mummification-and-life-afte.who_may: Mummies may animate, according to rumor.
mystara.rule.mummification-and-life-afte.combines: Mummies are placed in family crypts.
mystara.rule.mummification-and-life-afte.blocked_reason: The passage links death, continued existence, and reanimation without specifying a playable soul-state system.

mystara.rule.oenkmar-penal-code.name: Oenkmar penal code

effect.summary: The city has a penal code inspired by old Aengmorian writings, though enforcement favors powerful advocates.

mystara.rule.oenkmar-penal-code.cost_or_limit: Interpretation often depends on influence and intimidation.
mystara.rule.oenkmar-penal-code.go_wrong: Muscle and vocal force can override refined legal reasoning.
mystara.rule.oenkmar-penal-code.combines: Applied by lawyers such as the Tupacs.
mystara.rule.oenkmar-penal-code.blocked_reason: It describes a social legal mechanism, not an effect outside the grammar.

mystara.rule.priestly-food-dependence.name: Priestly food dependence

effect.summary: The military cannot readily overthrow the priesthood because many residents depend on priests to create food.

mystara.rule.priestly-food-dependence.cost_or_limit: The military faction’s authority is limited by reliance on priestly food supply.
mystara.rule.priestly-food-dependence.go_wrong: Resolving the food dependence could trigger civil war.
mystara.rule.priestly-food-dependence.combines: Keeps the military and priesthood in an uneasy truce.
mystara.rule.priestly-food-dependence.blocked_reason: This is a social constraint, not an unsupported supernatural effect.

mystara.rule.coming-of-age-ceremony.name: Coming of Age Ceremony

effect.summary: A teenager becomes an accepted tribesman by completing an ordeal and joining a clan.

mystara.rule.coming-of-age-ceremony.go_wrong: Failure or lack of a master may result in pariah status.
mystara.rule.coming-of-age-ceremony.mind: The new tribesman is expected to abandon family ties and serve a master.
mystara.rule.coming-of-age-ceremony.combines: Marks transition to Normal Monster status.
mystara.rule.coming-of-age-ceremony.blocked_reason: The rule concerns social status and can be handled without a missing effect capability.

mystara.rule.pariah-status.name: Pariah status

effect.summary: A tribesman without a master, or one who loses all retainers, becomes a shunned pariah.

mystara.rule.pariah-status.cost_or_limit: A pariah may remain in the horde but is treated as an outcast.
mystara.rule.pariah-status.go_wrong: A pariah with retainers must leave and form a separate horde.
mystara.rule.pariah-status.combines: A chief who loses all retainers suffers a lasting penalty to command attempts in that horde.

mystara.rule.retainers-and-tribal-author.name: Retainers and tribal authority

effect.summary: A character who gains retainers may become a chief, but taking followers can provoke reprisals or political rivalry.

mystara.rule.retainers-and-tribal-author.cost_or_limit: A horde chief may attack a subordinate who takes the chief’s retainers.
mystara.rule.retainers-and-tribal-author.go_wrong: A weakened chieftain may lose followers and become a pariah.

mystara.rule.chief-owns-everything-in-th.name: Chief owns everything in the horde

effect.summary: The chief is treated as owner of everything in the horde, provided subjects are not starved into rebellion or flight.

mystara.rule.chief-owns-everything-in-th.cost_or_limit: The chief must keep subjects fed enough to retain them.
mystara.rule.chief-owns-everything-in-th.go_wrong: Starvation can cause rebellion or desertion.
mystara.rule.chief-owns-everything-in-th.combines: Tribute may be demanded by tribal chiefs.
mystara.rule.chief-owns-everything-in-th.blocked_reason: It is a social property rule.

mystara.rule.humanoid-trade-and-tribute.name: Humanoid trade and tribute

effect.summary: Humanoids chiefly exchange goods; chiefs may demand occasional tribute, while treasure is mostly status or ritual wealth.

mystara.rule.humanoid-trade-and-tribute.cost_or_limit: Tribute may include food, equipment, slaves, cattle, troops, or labor.
mystara.rule.humanoid-trade-and-tribute.go_wrong: Refusing tribute can lead to war.
mystara.rule.humanoid-trade-and-tribute.combines: Goods are generally preferred to currency.

mystara.rule.horde-food-capacity.name: Horde food capacity

effect.summary: An ordinary eight-mile hex supports 50 HD of humanoids, with adjustments for water, riverbanks, fungal forests, and conventional forests.

mystara.rule.horde-food-capacity.cost_or_limit: Double capacity by a lake, riverbank, or fungal forest; halve it in a conventional forest; exclude specified barren terrain.
mystara.rule.horde-food-capacity.combines: Excess food and minerals can be traded.

mystara.rule.starvation-consequences.name: Starvation consequences

effect.summary: Food shortage can cause flight and death, reducing a horde’s population.

mystara.rule.starvation-consequences.cost_or_limit: At severe starvation, a chieftain has a 10% monthly chance to flee with a clan and 3d6 individuals flee or die weekly.
mystara.rule.starvation-consequences.go_wrong: A badly diminished horde may betray and remove its chief.
mystara.rule.starvation-consequences.combines: Raids and trade may temporarily relieve shortages.
mystara.rule.starvation-consequences.blocked_reason: The stated consequence is a population and vitality loss.

mystara.rule.food-exchange-values.name: Food exchange values

effect.summary: One gold piece buys a week of food for one HD of humanoids; one HD of cattle is valued at roughly 1–3 gp.

mystara.rule.food-exchange-values.cost_or_limit: Values vary with circumstances; trolls may need twice the food of other humanoids.
mystara.rule.food-exchange-values.combines: Used to estimate food trade and supply.

mystara.rule.combat-ready-horde-proporti.name: Combat-ready horde proportion

effect.summary: About three quarters of a horde is fit for combat; the remainder are too young or unable to fight.

mystara.rule.combat-ready-horde-proporti.cost_or_limit: The estimate includes adult males, females, teenagers, and elders.
mystara.rule.combat-ready-horde-proporti.go_wrong: Casualties can sharply reduce the horde’s population.
mystara.rule.combat-ready-horde-proporti.blocked_reason: It is a military accounting rule.

mystara.rule.war-machine-capacity-and-mo.name: War machine capacity and movement

effect.summary: A machine’s total weight must be pulled by enough of the horde; it moves only at walking speed in favorable conditions.

mystara.rule.war-machine-capacity-and-mo.cost_or_limit: A machine cannot move if the horde lacks sufficient pulling strength; at least one engineering leader and an artillery crew member per weapon are required.
mystara.rule.war-machine-capacity-and-mo.go_wrong: Trying to support more than one machine may exhaust the horde.
mystara.rule.war-machine-capacity-and-mo.combines: Tamed beasts may help pull it if acquired and trained.
mystara.rule.war-machine-capacity-and-mo.blocked_reason: It is a vehicle capacity rule.

mystara.rule.siege-damage-to-structures.name: Siege damage to structures

effect.summary: Siege weapons damage structures; most damage is halved against stone or metal, while ballistas deal fixed hull damage.

mystara.rule.siege-damage-to-structures.cost_or_limit: Damage depends on weapon size and construction material.

mystara.rule.demi-race-reproduction.name: Demi-race reproduction

effect.summary: Reproduction depends on parental size and HD difference; offspring race and traits are determined randomly.

mystara.rule.demi-race-reproduction.cost_or_limit: No offspring is expected if one parent is less than half the other’s size; base chance is 70%, reduced by 5% per HD difference to a minimum of 5%.
mystara.rule.demi-race-reproduction.go_wrong: Traits can be unpredictable and may be concealed by appearance.
mystara.rule.demi-race-reproduction.combines: Dice determine parent race and inherited features.
mystara.rule.demi-race-reproduction.blocked_reason: Generating a demi-race with mixed physical features requires form construction beyond the basic effect grammar.

mystara.rule.humanoid-aging.name: Humanoid aging

effect.summary: Humanoids mature at species-specific ages and gain or lose ability scores as they age.

mystara.rule.humanoid-aging.cost_or_limit: Age thresholds differ by species; aging modifiers cannot exceed ability-score or racial limits.
mystara.rule.humanoid-aging.go_wrong: Elders check constitution annually and may die of old age on a natural one.
mystara.rule.humanoid-aging.mind: Age may alter Wisdom and Intelligence.
mystara.rule.humanoid-aging.combines: Age progression is tracked over game years.
mystara.rule.humanoid-aging.blocked_reason: The described changes are attribute and lifespan adjustments.

mystara.rule.old-age-death.name: Old-age death

effect.summary: An elder who rolls a natural one on an annual Constitution check dies of old age.

mystara.rule.old-age-death.cost_or_limit: Applies to elders who use the optional age rules.
mystara.rule.old-age-death.go_wrong: Death occurs on the specified roll.
mystara.rule.old-age-death.combines: The annual check also represents age-related decline.
mystara.rule.old-age-death.blocked_reason: It is a straightforward triggered death rule.

mystara.rule.path-of-the-conqueror.name: Path of the Conqueror

effect.summary: A humanoid who completes the quest becomes an Immortal in their sphere of power.

mystara.rule.path-of-the-conqueror.cost_or_limit: The hero must meet the level or experience threshold and complete four major achievements involving a war machine, tribal control, population, and conquest.
mystara.rule.path-of-the-conqueror.go_wrong: Failure to complete the tasks prevents ascension.
mystara.rule.path-of-the-conqueror.mind: Requires dedication, bravery, persistence, and success at warfare.
mystara.rule.path-of-the-conqueror.who_may: Humanoids at level 30 or 1,000,000 XP, whichever comes first
mystara.rule.path-of-the-conqueror.combines: Requires an excellent war machine and victories in three battles.
mystara.rule.path-of-the-conqueror.blocked_reason: Becoming an Immortal changes the character’s soul or state of existence, which the basic effect grammar cannot model.

mystara.rule.oenkmarian-intelligence-and.name: Oenkmarian Intelligence and Wisdom adjustment

effect.summary: Oenkmarians have one-point-reduced penalties to Intelligence and Wisdom compared with common Broken Landers.

mystara.rule.oenkmarian-intelligence-and.mind: Improves these mental attributes relative to the usual penalties.
mystara.rule.oenkmarian-intelligence-and.blocked_reason: It is a direct mental attribute adjustment.

mystara.rule.humanoids-becoming-immortal.name: Humanoids becoming Immortals

effect.summary: A humanoid may start an Immortality quest at level 30 or one million experience points, whichever comes first.

mystara.rule.humanoids-becoming-immortal.cost_or_limit: The quest also requires dedication, warfare, and persistence.
mystara.rule.humanoids-becoming-immortal.go_wrong: Without the required achievements, the hero does not ascend.
mystara.rule.humanoids-becoming-immortal.combines: Leads to the Path of the Conqueror.

mystara.rule.the-temple-drains-power-thr.name: The temple drains power through the nightwing

effect.summary: The temple draws the energy needed to keep Oenkmar above the lava through the nightwing, a living portal to entropy.

mystara.rule.the-temple-drains-power-thr.cost_or_limit: The city depends on the connection.
mystara.rule.the-temple-drains-power-thr.go_wrong: Destroying the nightwing makes the city sink; freeing it eventually leaves the city immobilized.
mystara.rule.the-temple-drains-power-thr.combines: Nightwing, plane of entropy, temple, and city
mystara.rule.the-temple-drains-power-thr.blocked_reason: The rule requires a portal to transmit power into a city-sustaining system.

mystara.rule.sacrificed-victims-souls-an.name: Sacrificed victims’ souls and bodies

effect.summary: After sacrifice, a victim’s soul enters the pocket universe while the unconscious body stays on the material plane; raising the victim or defeating the herald can return them before serpents eat the body.

mystara.rule.sacrificed-victims-souls-an.cost_or_limit: The rescue must happen before the body is devoured.
mystara.rule.sacrificed-victims-souls-an.go_wrong: If devoured, the victim reincarnates as a feathered serpent; if the body is otherwise destroyed, the soul is stranded.
mystara.rule.sacrificed-victims-souls-an.mind: The victim is unconscious in the body during the separation.
mystara.rule.sacrificed-victims-souls-an.combines: Altar, pocket universe, raising, herald, and feathered serpents
mystara.rule.sacrificed-victims-souls-an.blocked_reason: This rule governs soul location, bodily death, rescue, and reincarnation.

mystara.rule.atzanteotl-s-bargain.name: Atzanteotl’s bargain

effect.summary: A deal restores the victim to the altar just after sacrifice and rewinds other characters and events to their state and location at that moment.

mystara.rule.atzanteotl-s-bargain.cost_or_limit: The victim must make a bargain requiring a quest for chaos and an alignment change.
mystara.rule.atzanteotl-s-bargain.go_wrong: The victim returns chaotic, and the rewind restores destroyed or stolen things and revives those killed in the interval.
mystara.rule.atzanteotl-s-bargain.mind: Characters remember events that are undone.
mystara.rule.atzanteotl-s-bargain.who_may: A stranded victim making a deal with Atzanteotl
mystara.rule.atzanteotl-s-bargain.combines: Reverses events for the victim’s party and surroundings
mystara.rule.atzanteotl-s-bargain.mechanism: Triggered local time rollback and state restoration
mystara.rule.atzanteotl-s-bargain.blocked_reason: The effect rewinds time and restores multiple entities and objects to prior states.

mystara.rule.ritual-sacrifice-of-clachtl.name: Ritual sacrifice of clachtli losers

effect.summary: Tradition calls for the losing team in clachtli to be sacrificed on Atzanteotl’s altar.

mystara.rule.ritual-sacrifice-of-clachtl.cost_or_limit: Applies traditionally to the losing team.
mystara.rule.ritual-sacrifice-of-clachtl.go_wrong: The losers face ritual death or the altar’s soul-transport effect.
mystara.rule.ritual-sacrifice-of-clachtl.blocked_reason: The connected sacrifice can separate souls from bodies and send them to another realm.

mystara.rule.duh-legion-s-sacred-laws.name: Duh Legion’s Sacred Laws

effect.summary: The Legion’s manual establishes rules of conduct and discipline for its warriors.

mystara.rule.duh-legion-s-sacred-laws.cost_or_limit: Warriors are expected to obey the chief and the manual.
mystara.rule.duh-legion-s-sacred-laws.go_wrong: Punishments are described for disobedience and disrespect.
mystara.rule.duh-legion-s-sacred-laws.blocked_reason: This is an organizational restriction and consequence, not a supernatural effect.

mystara.rule.chief-s-authority.name: Chief’s authority

effect.summary: Warriors and chieftains obey higher-ranking leaders, ultimately King Thar.

mystara.rule.chief-s-authority.cost_or_limit: The hierarchy runs from warrior to clan chieftain, Legion chief, and king.
mystara.rule.chief-s-authority.go_wrong: The manual describes punishment for disobedience.
mystara.rule.chief-s-authority.blocked_reason: This is a social rule that can be represented through ordinary faction procedures.

mystara.rule.tharian-code-orders.name: Tharian Code orders

effect.summary: The Legion’s commands are given in Tharian Code, and warriors are expected to understand and follow them.

mystara.rule.tharian-code-orders.cost_or_limit: The orders use the Legion’s warrior language and gestures.
mystara.rule.tharian-code-orders.go_wrong: Failure to understand may bring adverse assignments or punishment.
mystara.rule.tharian-code-orders.blocked_reason: This is a procedural social restriction, not a supernatural capability.

mystara.rule.disobedience-penalties.name: Disobedience penalties

effect.summary: Repeated disobedience brings escalating hanging penalties; disrespect toward leaders brings lashes or beheading.

mystara.rule.disobedience-penalties.cost_or_limit: Penalties escalate with repeat offenses and rank of the insulted leader.
mystara.rule.disobedience-penalties.who_may: Legion warriors are subject to the rule.
mystara.rule.disobedience-penalties.combines: Chiefly authority and the Legion’s conduct manual.
mystara.rule.disobedience-penalties.blocked_reason: The rule is representable as ordinary social consequences and harm.

mystara.rule.lost-equipment-penalty.name: Lost equipment penalty

effect.summary: A warrior who loses issued equipment forfeits their next loot share for replacements and receives lashes.

mystara.rule.lost-equipment-penalty.cost_or_limit: Replacement costs the next loot share plus ten lashes.
mystara.rule.lost-equipment-penalty.blocked_reason: This is an ordinary resource and punishment rule.

mystara.rule.warrior-pay-and-treasure-sh.name: Warrior pay and treasure sharing

effect.summary: Treasure is divided into shares by rank, size, and warrior group.

mystara.rule.warrior-pay-and-treasure-sh.cost_or_limit: Chiefs and chieftains receive priority; lesser troops can receive nothing if treasure runs short.
mystara.rule.warrior-pay-and-treasure-sh.go_wrong: Disputes use medal value to decide selection order.
mystara.rule.warrior-pay-and-treasure-sh.combines: Rank, clan size, and warrior type determine shares
mystara.rule.warrior-pay-and-treasure-sh.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward allocation rule.

mystara.rule.loot-concealment-prohibitio.name: Loot concealment prohibition

effect.summary: Warriors may not hide loot from the Legion after a raid.

mystara.rule.loot-concealment-prohibitio.cost_or_limit: First offense cuts off the ears; the second brings branding and banishment, with execution if the offender stays.
mystara.rule.loot-concealment-prohibitio.combines: Loot belongs to the king and Legion
mystara.rule.loot-concealment-prohibitio.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward legal consequence.

mystara.rule.personal-sacrifices.name: Personal Sacrifices

effect.summary: A sacrifice can cost permanent hit points or Constitution, while sometimes granting experience or an ability increase.

mystara.rule.personal-sacrifices.cost_or_limit: Possible losses include one or more permanent hit points or Constitution points.
mystara.rule.personal-sacrifices.go_wrong: A supernatural entity may demand payment; an omen can accompany the outcome.
mystara.rule.personal-sacrifices.combines: Immortals may approve or send an entity
mystara.rule.personal-sacrifices.mechanism: Ritual sacrifice with lasting stat changes
mystara.rule.personal-sacrifices.blocked_reason: The listed costs and rewards are direct character-state changes.

mystara.rule.natural-armor-class.name: Natural Armor Class

effect.summary: Humanoid species have listed natural armor values, modified by Dexterity and better armor.

mystara.rule.natural-armor-class.cost_or_limit: Armor matters only when its protection exceeds natural armor.
mystara.rule.natural-armor-class.combines: Dexterity and armor alter the result
mystara.rule.natural-armor-class.blocked_reason: This is a direct armor-rating rule.

mystara.rule.weapon-defects.name: Weapon Defects

effect.summary: Weapon failure outcomes can damage or destroy armor pieces and impair protection.

mystara.rule.weapon-defects.cost_or_limit: Results depend on the failure roll and damage.
mystara.rule.weapon-defects.go_wrong: Armor can fall off, rattle, need repair, or be destroyed.
mystara.rule.weapon-defects.combines: Armor and shields may be affected
mystara.rule.weapon-defects.blocked_reason: The rule describes ordinary item condition changes.

mystara.rule.unfortunate-legacy.name: Unfortunate Legacy

effect.summary: A character can acquire lasting afflictions such as addiction, allergies, disease, or phobias.

mystara.rule.unfortunate-legacy.cost_or_limit: Some results impose checks, penalties, or recurring effects.
mystara.rule.unfortunate-legacy.go_wrong: Multiple afflictions may be rolled together.
mystara.rule.unfortunate-legacy.mind: May include compulsions, phobias, or impaired senses.
mystara.rule.unfortunate-legacy.blocked_reason: The listed afflictions fit standard condition and trait rules.

mystara.rule.partial-armor-ratings.name: Partial Armor Ratings

effect.summary: Armor pieces contribute partial ratings that are combined to calculate final armor class.

mystara.rule.partial-armor-ratings.cost_or_limit: Add partial ratings, divide by ten, round down, and subtract from nine.
mystara.rule.partial-armor-ratings.combines: Material and covered body parts determine rating
mystara.rule.partial-armor-ratings.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward equipment calculation.

mystara.rule.borderlands-freehold-rule.name: Borderlands freehold rule

effect.summary: Freehold residents owe loyalty and taxes to their Magistrate, who protects them; an heir assumes the title when a Magistrate dies.

mystara.rule.borderlands-freehold-rule.cost_or_limit: Magistrates generally govern freely unless they commit grave crimes.

mystara.rule.merchant-s-guild-credit-bac.name: Merchant’s Guild credit backing

effect.summary: Guild credit may rely on its reputation or be backed by stored cash.

mystara.rule.merchant-s-guild-credit-bac.cost_or_limit: Only some issued credit has cash reserves behind it.
mystara.rule.merchant-s-guild-credit-bac.combines: Credit instruments and the Guild's cash holdings.

mystara.rule.the-khan-owns-all-the-wealt.name: The Khan owns all the wealth of the tribe

effect.summary: Tribal possessions, including newly born animals, belong to the Khan.

mystara.rule.marriage-within-the-same-cl.name: Marriage within the same clan is not allowed

effect.summary: Members of one clan may not marry each other.

mystara.rule.ethengar-year-cycle.name: Ethengar year cycle

effect.summary: The Ethengars use a twelve-year cycle in which each year is named for an animal.

mystara.rule.ethengar-year-cycle.cost_or_limit: A person’s birth year matters more astrologically than their birth month.
mystara.rule.ethengar-year-cycle.combines: Each year has a spirit companion watching over those born in it.

mystara.rule.spirit-companion.name: spirit companion

effect.summary: Every year has an animal spirit companion assigned to watch over all creatures born in that year.

mystara.rule.spirit-companion.cost_or_limit: One companion corresponds to each year in the cycle.
mystara.rule.spirit-companion.who_may: All creatures born in the year
mystara.rule.spirit-companion.where_from: A decree of the Great Spirit

mystara.rule.chosen-horse-spirit.name: chosen horse spirit

effect.summary: Guiding a chosen horse’s spirit to the Spirit World assures success in breeding and training the tribe’s horses for months.

mystara.rule.chosen-horse-spirit.who_may: A tribe whose shamans perform the rite
mystara.rule.chosen-horse-spirit.combines: The horse spirit watches over the tribal herds.

mystara.rule.spirit-world-access.name: Spirit World access

effect.summary: Known World travelers need the Black Sand gate or high-level spells to reach the Spirit World.

mystara.rule.spirit-world-access.cost_or_limit: The gate or high-level magic is required.
mystara.rule.spirit-world-access.go_wrong: The gate route is guarded and crosses hostile territory.
mystara.rule.spirit-world-access.who_may: Travelers with the required route or magic; a shaman enables a group to pass the guardians.
mystara.rule.spirit-world-access.combines: The gate is on the World Mountain in the Land of Black Sand.
mystara.rule.spirit-world-access.blocked_reason: This is a travel restriction rather than a basic-grammar effect.

mystara.rule.spirit-guide-bond-and-loss.name: Spirit guide bond and loss

effect.summary: A shaman's guide shares the shaman's combat statistics, acts independently, and cannot travel far away.

mystara.rule.spirit-guide-bond-and-loss.cost_or_limit: The guide has a limited distance from the shaman.
mystara.rule.spirit-guide-bond-and-loss.go_wrong: If slain in the Spirit World, the shaman temporarily loses half their experience level until the guide returns.
mystara.rule.spirit-guide-bond-and-loss.combines: A replacement guide is received after a month of meditation and prayer in the World Yurt.
mystara.rule.spirit-guide-bond-and-loss.mechanism: Bound companion with a death penalty and recovery period.
mystara.rule.spirit-guide-bond-and-loss.blocked_reason: The companion bond, distance limit, and linked death penalty are not expressible as a basic effect.

mystara.rule.summoned-spirit-duration-an.name: Summoned spirit duration and damage

effect.summary: Summoned spirits return when a spell ends, retain damage across repeat castings that day, and recover hit points in the Spirit World.

mystara.rule.summoned-spirit-duration-an.cost_or_limit: They regain 2d6 hit points per day in the Spirit World and may also be healed by spells.
mystara.rule.summoned-spirit-duration-an.go_wrong: At zero hit points outside the Spirit World they return weakened; at zero inside it they die permanently.
mystara.rule.summoned-spirit-duration-an.where_from: The Spirit World and the summoning spell.
mystara.rule.summoned-spirit-duration-an.combines: A shaman whose spirits die in the Spirit World must meditate for 1d4 weeks before summoning again.
mystara.rule.summoned-spirit-duration-an.mechanism: Summon duration, persistent damage, recovery, and permanent death.
mystara.rule.summoned-spirit-duration-an.blocked_reason: Persistent companion condition and permanent death cannot be represented by the basic effect grammar.

mystara.rule.animal-spirit-deaths.name: Animal spirit deaths

effect.summary: A summoned spirit reduced to zero hit points outside the Spirit World returns there; one reduced to zero within it dies and cannot be restored.

mystara.rule.animal-spirit-deaths.cost_or_limit: A shaman must meditate 1d4 weeks after spirits die in the Spirit World before summoning again.
mystara.rule.animal-spirit-deaths.go_wrong: Death in the Spirit World is permanent; raising and reincarnation do not work.
mystara.rule.animal-spirit-deaths.who_may: Applies to summoned spirits and their shaman.
mystara.rule.animal-spirit-deaths.combines: Spirits can recover hit points while in the Spirit World.
mystara.rule.animal-spirit-deaths.blocked_reason: Permanent death and recovery restrictions are soul-state mechanics.

mystara.rule.clan-event-table.name: Clan event table

effect.summary: At the start of each game year, a table roll determines a clan event that may change its status.

mystara.rule.clan-event-table.cost_or_limit: A clan can increase at most two levels per year, one from the event table and one from a character's performance.
mystara.rule.clan-event-table.go_wrong: Events may harm livestock or clan status.
mystara.rule.clan-event-table.who_may: Player characters associated with a clan.
mystara.rule.clan-event-table.combines: Events include grazing, feuds, raids, spirits, and other circumstances.
mystara.rule.clan-event-table.mechanism: Annual random event and status adjustment.
mystara.rule.clan-event-table.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure, not an effect requiring a missing capability.

mystara.rule.fourth-failed-saving-throw.name: Fourth failed saving throw

effect.summary: A character goes mad on the fourth failed saving throw.

mystara.rule.fourth-failed-saving-throw.combines: The madness may take forms drawn from fear, confusion, confound, or madness spells
mystara.rule.fourth-failed-saving-throw.blocked_reason: A threshold of failed saves and a resulting mental state can be tracked directly.

mystara.rule.madness-wears-off.name: Madness wears off

effect.summary: Madness effects end after 1d3 hours once characters reach the Sea of Grass.

mystara.rule.madness-wears-off.cost_or_limit: Requires reaching the Sea of Grass; lasts 1d3 hours
mystara.rule.madness-wears-off.go_wrong: Those who went insane retain recurring bad dreams
mystara.rule.madness-wears-off.mind: The immediate madness ends, but some characters have nightmares
mystara.rule.madness-wears-off.combines: Separate from the lingering dreams of characters who went insane
mystara.rule.madness-wears-off.blocked_reason: A timed condition can be implemented with the basic effect grammar.

mystara.rule.recurring-bad-dreams.name: Recurring bad dreams

effect.summary: Insane characters have nightmares every 2d10 nights and wake screaming.

mystara.rule.recurring-bad-dreams.go_wrong: Once, a dreamer may be caught and carried into the Spirit World
mystara.rule.recurring-bad-dreams.mind: The dreams involve pursuit by evil spirits and undead
mystara.rule.recurring-bad-dreams.combines: A dreamer may be taken into the Spirit World
mystara.rule.recurring-bad-dreams.blocked_reason: The passage allows a dream event to carry a character into another spiritual state or realm.

mystara.rule.blood-sustains-the-minor-ga.name: Blood sustains the minor gate

effect.summary: The pool’s minor gate stays open only while fed blood.

mystara.rule.blood-sustains-the-minor-ga.cost_or_limit: Requires blood to keep the gate open
mystara.rule.blood-sustains-the-minor-ga.go_wrong: The gate closes if not fed
mystara.rule.blood-sustains-the-minor-ga.where_from: The pool in the Black Sand
mystara.rule.blood-sustains-the-minor-ga.combines: The gate leads to Sphere Entropy
mystara.rule.blood-sustains-the-minor-ga.blocked_reason: The gate’s sustaining cost and failure condition are directly playable.

mystara.rule.turning-undead-in-the-black.name: Turning undead in the Black Sand

effect.summary: A cleric’s effective level for turning undead is reduced by two levels in the Black Sand.

mystara.rule.turning-undead-in-the-black.cost_or_limit: Two-level penalty; at the edge a first-level cleric can turn undead
mystara.rule.turning-undead-in-the-black.combines: The penalty applies to turning undead
mystara.rule.turning-undead-in-the-black.blocked_reason: A numeric penalty to an ability can be applied directly.

mystara.rule.drugged-drinks.name: Drugged drinks

effect.summary: A failed saving throw causes deep sleep for 1d4 hours.

mystara.rule.drugged-drinks.cost_or_limit: Requires failing a saving throw; sleep lasts 1d4 hours
mystara.rule.drugged-drinks.go_wrong: The affected character becomes helpless while asleep
mystara.rule.drugged-drinks.combines: Taijits use the drug to steal the box
mystara.rule.drugged-drinks.blocked_reason: A save-triggered, timed sleep effect can be represented directly.

mystara.rule.radiance-drain.name: Radiance drain

effect.summary: The Nucleus permanently drains magic from the Prime Material Plane, with the drain increasing over time.

mystara.rule.radiance-drain.cost_or_limit: The drain is permanent and gradually intensifies.
mystara.rule.radiance-drain.go_wrong: It will ultimately destroy all magic.
mystara.rule.radiance-drain.combines: Caused by the Nucleus's connection to the Sphere of Energy.
mystara.rule.radiance-drain.blocked_reason: The rule requires a persistent, increasing drain rather than a single basic effect.

mystara.rule.water-vortex-draws-matter-f.name: Water vortex draws matter from the Elemental Plane of Water

effect.summary: A vortex pulls material from the Elemental Plane of Water into the Warrens, polluting the water.

mystara.rule.water-vortex-draws-matter-f.cost_or_limit: The amount drawn in varies by round
mystara.rule.water-vortex-draws-matter-f.combines: Pollution attracts or irritates creatures in the area.
mystara.rule.water-vortex-draws-matter-f.blocked_reason: The passage describes a continuing planar transfer that the basic effect grammar cannot model in full.

mystara.rule.totem-selection-restriction.name: Totem selection restriction

effect.summary: Player characters cannot choose an intelligent creature as a totem.

mystara.rule.totem-selection-restriction.cost_or_limit: The Dungeon Master settles uncertain cases.
mystara.rule.totem-selection-restriction.who_may: Player characters are subject to the restriction.
mystara.rule.totem-selection-restriction.blocked_reason: The restriction is directly usable as a game rule.

mystara.rule.starting-age.name: Starting age

effect.summary: Atruaghin characters begin at age twelve plus a random one to four years.

mystara.rule.starting-age.blocked_reason: The age rule can be applied directly.

mystara.rule.magic-use-among-the-atruagh.name: Magic use among the Atruaghin Clans

effect.summary: Clan-born magic-users gain experience at half the normal rate while adventuring in clan territory.

mystara.rule.magic-use-among-the-atruagh.cost_or_limit: The reduced rate applies within Atruaghin territory.
mystara.rule.magic-use-among-the-atruagh.where_from: Their limited access to outside magical learning.
mystara.rule.magic-use-among-the-atruagh.blocked_reason: The passage gives a direct, usable limit on character advancement.

mystara.rule.shamani-magic-can-be-withdr.name: Shamani magic can be withdrawn

effect.summary: A shamani who betrays or fails the tribes may suddenly lose their magic.

mystara.rule.shamani-magic-can-be-withdr.cost_or_limit: The loss may occur without warning.
mystara.rule.shamani-magic-can-be-withdr.go_wrong: Magic is stripped from an unfaithful or failing shamani.
mystara.rule.shamani-magic-can-be-withdr.blocked_reason: The rule removes a character’s powers, which the basic effect grammar cannot model as a power-state change.

mystara.rule.makaki-creation-requires-th.name: Makaki creation requires the totem hunt

effect.summary: A character must find and kill their own totem animal without shamani magic before crafting a medicine bundle.

mystara.rule.makaki-creation-requires-th.cost_or_limit: The heart and ashes are required, along with six associated items and a full-moon ceremony.
mystara.rule.makaki-creation-requires-th.go_wrong: The ceremony drains 1d4 hit points from the supplicant.
mystara.rule.makaki-creation-requires-th.blocked_reason: This is a crafting and resource-cost rule.

mystara.rule.children-of-atruaghin-may-n.name: Children of Atruaghin may not kill one another

effect.summary: Atruaghin’s code forbids members of the tribes from killing each other.

mystara.rule.children-of-atruaghin-may-n.go_wrong: A fatal coup attacker must accompany the victim’s body in the funeral boat or be captured and sent helplessly.
mystara.rule.children-of-atruaghin-may-n.blocked_reason: This is a world-law restriction on lethal conduct.

mystara.rule.bear-clan-healing-glaze.name: Bear Clan healing glaze

effect.summary: Wounded people resting in a Bear Clan home heal at twice their usual rate.

mystara.rule.bear-clan-healing-glaze.cost_or_limit: Applies to wounded people resting inside a Bear Clan home.
mystara.rule.bear-clan-healing-glaze.where_from: The sacred clay glaze on Bear Clan buildings.
mystara.rule.bear-clan-healing-glaze.combines: The glaze is made by Bear Clan shamani and applied to buildings.
mystara.rule.bear-clan-healing-glaze.blocked_reason: The rule describes a straightforward change to the rate of recovery.

mystara.rule.bear-clan-chief-s-term.name: Bear Clan chief's term

effect.summary: The chief is elected yearly and rules by consent, subject to removal by a confidence vote or disabling injury.

mystara.rule.bear-clan-chief-s-term.cost_or_limit: A confidence vote that supports the chief forces its initiator to leave the tribe until the next regular election.
mystara.rule.bear-clan-chief-s-term.go_wrong: A removed chief becomes a wanderer and may die during exile.
mystara.rule.bear-clan-chief-s-term.who_may: Bear Clan citizens can call for a confidence vote.
mystara.rule.bear-clan-chief-s-term.where_from: Children of the Bear governance custom.
mystara.rule.bear-clan-chief-s-term.combines: The highest-ranking local shamani must affirm that Atruaghin is pleased with the chief's reign.
mystara.rule.bear-clan-chief-s-term.blocked_reason: The governance constraints can be run as ordinary world rules.

mystara.rule.bear-clan-metal-farming-too.name: Bear Clan metal farming tools

effect.summary: Bear Clan farmers reject metal tools because they believe these tools poison the soil.

mystara.rule.bear-clan-metal-farming-too.cost_or_limit: Applies to farming tools; wooden and stone tools are used instead.
mystara.rule.bear-clan-metal-farming-too.go_wrong: The asserted soil poisoning is a belief, not confirmed as an actual effect.
mystara.rule.bear-clan-metal-farming-too.who_may: Children of the Bear refuse to use such tools.
mystara.rule.bear-clan-metal-farming-too.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward restriction on tool use.

mystara.rule.golden-one-challenge.name: golden one challenge

effect.summary: A family challenge is settled by negotiating a barter price for a specially cast golden figure; accepting the offer is expected.

mystara.rule.golden-one-challenge.cost_or_limit: The challenger sets a negotiation date, customarily 2–7 days after the offer.
mystara.rule.golden-one-challenge.go_wrong: If no deal is reached, both families are disgraced to some degree.
mystara.rule.golden-one-challenge.who_may: Turtle Clan families may challenge one another.
mystara.rule.golden-one-challenge.combines: The shamani oversee the casting and witness the final transaction.
mystara.rule.golden-one-challenge.blocked_reason: This is a social procedure that can be resolved through ordinary play.

mystara.rule.golden-one-combat-bonus.name: golden one combat bonus

effect.summary: A family head who owns golden ones gains one bonus hit die per figure when entering combat or a hunt.

mystara.rule.golden-one-combat-bonus.cost_or_limit: Only applies to the head of a family possessing at least one golden one; does not improve attacks or level-based abilities.
mystara.rule.golden-one-combat-bonus.who_may: The head of a family with golden ones.
mystara.rule.golden-one-combat-bonus.combines: The number of bonus hit dice equals the number of figures held.
mystara.rule.golden-one-combat-bonus.blocked_reason: The bonus is granted by owned objects, so the item-linked benefit is not represented by the basic effect grammar.

mystara.rule.turtle-clan-social-classes.name: Turtle Clan social classes

effect.summary: Family status can shift among the recognized social classes according to fortune and conduct, while noshaki status is fixed.

mystara.rule.turtle-clan-social-classes.cost_or_limit: Noshaki cannot marry, have children, own property, or rise to another class.
mystara.rule.turtle-clan-social-classes.who_may: Children of the Turtle families and people without families are classified by these customs.
mystara.rule.turtle-clan-social-classes.combines: Patshatl celebrations can improve a family's standing for a time.
mystara.rule.turtle-clan-social-classes.blocked_reason: Social status and its restrictions can be represented directly as world rules.

mystara.rule.turtle-clan-marriage-transf.name: Turtle Clan marriage transfer

effect.summary: A person may leave their family to join a spouse's family, commonly to enter one of higher status.

mystara.rule.turtle-clan-marriage-transf.cost_or_limit: The transfer is accompanied by gifts and promises of loyalty, with feasts held by both families.
mystara.rule.turtle-clan-marriage-transf.where_from: Children of the Turtle marriage custom.
mystara.rule.turtle-clan-marriage-transf.combines: A family transfer may change the person's social standing.
mystara.rule.turtle-clan-marriage-transf.blocked_reason: The described change in family affiliation is a social relation rather than a power transfer.

mystara.rule.turtle-clan-property-and-la.name: Turtle Clan property and land

effect.summary: Ownership principally means the right to use; land can be hunted, fished, or farmed rather than individually owned.

mystara.rule.turtle-clan-property-and-la.cost_or_limit: All land, objects, and slaves are treated as belonging to the current chief, who annually grants people leave to keep and use newly acquired things.
mystara.rule.turtle-clan-property-and-la.who_may: The chief grants use to the tribe's people.
mystara.rule.turtle-clan-property-and-la.where_from: Children of the Turtle property custom.
mystara.rule.turtle-clan-property-and-la.combines: Annual accounting and grants take place at the winter-solstice festival.
mystara.rule.turtle-clan-property-and-la.mechanism: communal use rights and annual allocation
mystara.rule.turtle-clan-property-and-la.blocked_reason: The rule describes ownership and permission as social relations.

mystara.rule.totem-pole-protection.name: totem pole protection

effect.summary: A house's totem poles ward off evil spirits; if a shamani of at least name level oversees their raising, the house protects everyone inside as a protection from evil spell.

mystara.rule.totem-pole-protection.cost_or_limit: The magical protection requires oversight by a shamani of at least name level.
mystara.rule.totem-pole-protection.go_wrong: Failure to expand or abandon a house when its poles are filled with carvings is rumored to draw the Immortals' wrath.
mystara.rule.totem-pole-protection.who_may: The protection benefits people inside the house.
mystara.rule.totem-pole-protection.where_from: Turtle Clan totem-pole custom and the Immortals.
mystara.rule.totem-pole-protection.combines: The house's poles begin with images of the founder's totem and the clan's immortal turtle spirit.
mystara.rule.totem-pole-protection.blocked_reason: The spell-like protection applies to all occupants within a house, requiring a persistent area effect.
